newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK CPI (A) rises annual 6.7 pct in December.
newsitem.headline: HK CPI (A) rises annual 6.7 pct in December.

text.p: The Census and Statistics Department released the following consumer price index data showing Hong Kong's CPI (A) rose 6.7 percent in December year-on-year.
CPI (A) rose six percent in 1996 overall, it said.
CPI (A), Hong Kong's broadest measure of inflation, is based on the 50 percent of households spending between HK$4,000 and HK$15,999 a month as of the 1994/95 fiscal year base.
CPI (B) is based on the 30 percent of households which spend HK$16,000 to HK$29,999 a month as of the 1994/95 fiscal year base.
Hang Seng CPI Dec '96 Nov '96 Dec '95
The Hang Seng CPI, published by the Hang Seng Bank Ltd, is based on the 10 percent of households spending HK$30,000 to HK$59,999 as of the 1994/95 fiscal year base.
The composite CPI is based on the combined expenditure pattern of households covered by the three CPI's.
